name: Benjamin Harrison
blurb: 23rd US president (1833–1901) · installed the White House's first electric lighting but was so wary of it he left the switches to staff, sometimes letting the lights burn all night rather than touch one
source: Wikimedia Commons: Benjamin Harrison, head and shoulders bw photo, 1896.jpg

name: Deng Xiaoping
blurb: Paramount leader of Communist China (1904–1997) · donned a ten-gallon cowboy hat at a Texas rodeo during his landmark 1979 US tour, producing one of the era's most-reproduced photos
source: Wikimedia Commons: Deng Xiaoping and Jimmy Carter at the arrival ceremony for the Vice Premier of China. - NARA - 183157-restored(cropped).jpg

name: Rumi
blurb: Persian poet and Sufi mystic (1207–1273) · loose modern English translations of his verses made him the best-selling poet in the United States by the early 2000s
source: Wikimedia Commons: مولانا اثر حسین بهزاد (cropped).jpg

name: Cyrus the Great
blurb: Founder of the Achaemenid Persian Empire (c. 600–530 BC) · the Cyrus Cylinder, sometimes called history's first human-rights charter, records his policy of letting conquered peoples keep their own gods and customs
source: Wikimedia Commons: Great Men and Famous Women Volume 1 - Cyrus the Great.png

name: T. S. Eliot
blurb: American-British poet and critic (1888–1965) · spent eight years clocking in at Lloyds Bank in London while writing 'The Waste Land' on the side
attribution: Lady Ottoline Morrell; derivative work: Octave.H
source: Wikimedia Commons: Thomas Stearns Eliot by Lady Ottoline Morrell (1934).jpg
image_author: Lady Ottoline Morrell; derivative work: Octave.H

name: Charles Manson
blurb: American cult leader and convicted murderer (1934–2017) · carved a swastika into his own forehead during his 1970 murder trial, later reshaping it into an X
attribution: California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation
source: Wikimedia Commons: MansonB33920 8-14-17 (cropped).jpg
image_author: California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation

name: Martin Van Buren
blurb: 8th US president (1782–1862) · the first president born a US citizen rather than a British subject, and possibly the source of 'OK' via his nickname 'Old Kinderhook'
attribution: Mathew Benjamin Brady / Levin Corbin Handy
source: Wikimedia Commons: Martin Van Buren.jpg
image_author: Mathew Benjamin Brady / Levin Corbin Handy

name: Richard Feynman
blurb: American theoretical physicist (1918–1988) · cracked colleagues' safes for fun at Los Alamos during the Manhattan Project, sometimes leaving notes inside to spook them
source: Wikimedia Commons: RichardFeynman-PaineMansionWoods1984 copyrightTamikoThiel bw.jpg

name: Jeffrey Epstein
blurb: American financier and convicted sex offender (1953–2019) · a lenient 2008 plea deal let him serve just 13 months in a county jail, with generous work-release, before his 2019 federal re-arrest
source: Wikimedia Commons: Epstein 2013 mugshot.jpg

name: Joseph Smith
blurb: American religious leader and founder of the Latter Day Saint movement (1805–1844) · said he translated the Book of Mormon by staring at a seer stone placed inside his hat
source: Wikimedia Commons: Joseph Smith, Jr. (1843 photograph).jpg

name: Augusto Pinochet
blurb: Chilean military dictator (1915–2006) · was arrested in London in 1998 on a Spanish extradition warrant while recovering from back surgery
attribution: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Chile
source: Wikimedia Commons: Augusto Pinochet foto oficial (cropped)(2).jpg
image_author: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Chile

name: Ayn Rand
blurb: Russian-American novelist and philosopher (1905–1982) · a six-foot floral arrangement shaped like a dollar sign stood by her casket at her 1982 funeral
attribution: Photo portrait credited to "Talbot" (though not on original dust jacket). Published by the Bobbs-Merrill Company.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Ayn Rand (1943 Talbot portrait).jpg

name: Henry V of England
blurb: King of England (1386–1422) · his heavily outnumbered army's win over the French at Agincourt in 1415 was later immortalised in Shakespeare's play bearing his name
source: Wikimedia Commons: Henry V Miniature.jpg

name: Hannibal
blurb: Carthaginian general (247–183 BC) · marched dozens of war elephants across the Alps into Italy, though most did not survive the crossing
source: Wikimedia Commons: Mommsen p265.jpg

name: Zachary Taylor
blurb: 12th US president (1784–1850) · a career army officer who had never once voted in a presidential election before winning one himself
attribution: unknown, possibly Maguire of New Orleans; derivative work: Beao
source: Wikimedia Commons: Zachary Taylor restored and cropped.jpg
image_author: unknown, possibly Maguire of New Orleans; derivative work: Beao

name: John Steinbeck
blurb: American novelist (1902–1968) · won the 1962 Nobel Prize in Literature despite a scathing New York Times editorial questioning whether he deserved it
attribution: McFadden Publications, Inc.; no photographer credited; photo likely the work of Sonya Noskowiak, as Steinbeck is wearing the same clothes from her 1935 studio session that produced the work shown here: https://www.si.edu/object/npg_NPG.2006.74
source: Wikimedia Commons: John Steinbeck 1939 (cropped).jpg

name: John D. Rockefeller
blurb: American oil magnate and philanthropist (1839–1937) · became history's first confirmed billionaire, with Standard Oil controlling some 90% of US oil refining at its peak
source: Wikimedia Commons: John-D-Rockefeller-sen.jpg

name: Pablo Escobar
blurb: Colombian drug lord (1949–1993) · Forbes listed him among the world's wealthiest people for seven straight years, with a peak net worth estimated near $30 billion
source: Wikimedia Commons: Pablo Escobar Mug.jpg

name: James K. Polk
blurb: 11th US president (1795–1849) · pledged to serve only one term, achieved every major goal he set for it, then died just months after leaving office
source: Wikimedia Commons: JamesKnoxPolk.jpg

name: Arthur Miller
blurb: American playwright (1915–2005) · was briefly married to Marilyn Monroe and wrote The Misfits as a screen vehicle for her
source: Wikimedia Commons: Arthur Miller by Wolfgang Fischer-01.jpg

name: Vivien Leigh
blurb: English actress (1913–1967) · beat out well over a thousand other actresses screen-tested for the role of Scarlett O'Hara in Gone with the Wind
source: Wikimedia Commons: Vivien Leigh Scarlet.jpg

name: Herodotus
blurb: Greek historian (c. 484–425 BC) · dubbed 'the Father of History' by Cicero, though critics in his own time called him 'the Father of Lies' for his tall tales
source: Wikimedia Commons: Marble bust of Herodotos MET DT11742 (cropped).jpg
